metadata.vintage: Confirmed from CHFA's official Dates and Deadlines page (chfainfo.com/rental-housing/housing-credit/dates-and-deadlines) on 2026-06-03; 2027 dates, QAP hearings and comment deadline re-verified 2026-09-24 against CHFA's QAP page (chfainfo.com/rental-housing/housing-credit/qualified-allocation-plan), its hearing notice (chfainfo.com/rental-housing/housing-credit/qap-hearing), the 2027-28 QAP Third Draft (section 3.B.2) and Third Draft Summary of Changes dated 2026-09-11, and the August 26, 2026 hearing presentation. On 2026-10-24 CHFA's QAP page still listed the Third Draft as the latest 2027-28 document (no adopted plan posted), and its hearing page (chfainfo.com/rental-housing/housing-credit/qap-hearing) announced the October 29 MIHTC and November 2 TOC and TZ Credit allocation plan hearings; that page no longer shows the July-August QAP hearings, which are kept here from the 2026-09-24 check. CHFA's published cycle: R1 = 9% + State Credit (Feb deadline); R2 = 4% + State Credit (Aug deadline). Pure 4% deals are rolling; R2 specifically targets 4%-with-State-Credit projects. MIHTC has its own annual deadline.

2027-28-qap-adopted.title: CHFA 2027-28 QAP, section 3.B.2 (adopted by the CHFA Board September 25, 2026; approved by the Governor October 23, 2026)

chfa-dates-and-deadlines-2026.title: CHFA Dates and Deadlines (2026 rounds, under the adopted 2025-26 QAP)

notes: Round 1 = 9% LIHTC + State Credit (highly competitive; February application)
Round 2 = 4% LIHTC + State Credit (4% paired with State Credit; August application). Pure 4% / PAB is rolling outside this cycle.
MIHTC (Middle Income Housing Tax Credit) is annual with its own LOI/app cycle (March/May)
Every CHFA round requires a Letter of Intent (LOI) 60+ days before the application — LOI deadlines are the real first gate

Prop 123's State Affordable Housing Fund is split: 60% is overseen by OEDIT and managed by CHFA (the Affordable Housing Financing Fund: land banking, equity, concessionary debt including LIHTC gap finance), and 40% goes to DOLA (the Affordable Housing Support Fund: homeownership, homelessness, local planning capacity). Each program has its own cycle, separate from CHFA's tax-credit rounds — see cdola.colorado.gov/prop123.

The QAP covers two years (2027-2028) and is the plan that sets cycle dates, credit maximums and scoring; it is drafted January-June, taken to public hearings and written comment in July-August, then goes to the CHFA Board and the Governor in September-October (CHFA's own timeline, August 26, 2026 hearing presentation).

2027 and 2028 round dates come from the 2027-28 QAP, adopted by the CHFA Board on September 25, 2026 and approved by the Governor on October 23, 2026 (posted October 30, 2026); its dates match the Third Draft. That adoption status is carried separately from date_precision: each round event has qap_status ("draft" or "adopted") and qap_source, a key into metadata.qap_sources, which names the document and the date it was verified. When CHFA adopts the plan, set that source's status and the events' qap_status to "adopted".

status is a snapshot as of metadata.generated. js/components/qap-calendar.js also compares each event's date (or date_end, when present) with today, so an event whose date has passed renders as past even if this field has not been refreshed.

events.name: 2027-28 QAP draft — first public hearing (Zoom)
events.details: First of three CHFA public hearings on the draft 2027-2028 Housing Tax Credit QAP, Tuesday July 14, 2026 at 11:00am via Zoom. The QAP now covers two years, 2027 and 2028.

events.name: 2027-28 QAP draft — second public hearing (Zoom)
events.details: Second public hearing on the draft 2027-2028 QAP, Thursday July 16, 2026 at 1:00pm via Zoom.

events.name: 2027-28 QAP draft — written comments due
events.details: CHFA accepted written comments on the draft 2027-2028 QAP up to August 14, 2026. Among the proposed changes: a Pilot Coordinated Funding and Concurrent Awards section that pairs competitive 2027 and 2028 tax-credit awards with state gap funding from the Division of Housing (DOH) and OEDIT.

events.name: 2027-28 QAP draft — third public hearing (Zoom)
events.details: Third public hearing on the draft 2027-2028 QAP, Wednesday August 26, 2026 at 10:00am via Zoom. CHFA then posted a Third Draft and Summary of Changes dated September 11, 2026.

events.name: 2027-28 QAP — CHFA Board approval, then Governor approval
events.details: The CHFA Board adopted the 2027-2028 QAP on September 25, 2026 and the Governor approved it on October 23, 2026 (cover page of the adopted plan). CHFA posted it on October 30, 2026. Checked 2026-11-01 against the adopted PDF: the round dates in section 3.B.2, the credit maximums in 3.L and 3.L.1, and the 3.B.9 gap pilot match the Third Draft.

events.name: 2027 MIHTC Allocation Plan draft — public hearing (Zoom)
events.details: CHFA public hearing on the draft 2027 Middle-income Housing Tax Credit (MIHTC) Allocation Plan, Thursday October 29, 2026, 10:00-11:00am via Zoom (registration link on CHFA's hearing page). CHFA accepts written comments up to the hearing date. The draft plan and its summary of changes are on CHFA's MIHTC page (chfainfo.com/rental-housing/housing-credit/middle-income-housing-tax-credit-mihtc). Checked 2026-10-24.

events.name: 2027 TOC Credit Allocation Plan draft — public hearing (Zoom)
events.details: CHFA public hearing on the draft 2027 Transit-oriented Communities (TOC) Credit Allocation Plan, Monday November 2, 2026, 2:00-3:00pm via Zoom (registration link on CHFA's hearing page). CHFA accepts written comments up to the hearing date. The draft plan and its summary of changes are on CHFA's state credit page (chfainfo.com/state-credit). Checked 2026-10-24.

events.name: 2027 TZ Credit Allocation Plan draft — public hearing (Zoom)

rolling_programs.name: 4% LIHTC + PAB (Private Activity Bond)
rolling_programs.description: 4% Tax-Exempt Bond financing is reviewed on a rolling basis: preliminary applications are accepted all year except February, August and December (2027-28 QAP, section 3.B.2, p. 16). Limited by annual PAB allocation — see data/pab-allocations.json for current year's available cap.

rolling_programs.name: MIHTC (Middle Income Housing Tax Credit)
rolling_programs.description: State-only Middle Income tax credit serving 80-120% AMI. Annual cycle typically R1-aligned. Small allocation; competitive.

rolling_programs.name: Colorado State LIHTC
rolling_programs.description: State tax credit MUST be paired with federal 9% or 4%. Same cycles as federal. Roughly doubles equity yield on stacked deals. Transit Zone (TZ) credit (HB26-1065) may be awarded in lieu of standard state credit under a separate TZ Credit Allocation Plan, within the same fixed state-credit amounts (2027-28 QAP as adopted, sections 3.B.2 and 3.L).

rolling_programs.name: Proposition 123 — Affordable Housing Fund
rolling_programs.description: Prop 123's State Affordable Housing Fund is split: 60% is overseen by OEDIT and managed by CHFA (the Affordable Housing Financing Fund: land banking, equity, concessionary debt including LIHTC gap finance), and 40% goes to DOLA (the Affordable Housing Support Fund: homeownership, homelessness, local planning capacity). Each program has its own cycle, separate from CHFA's tax-credit rounds. DOLA's Prop 123 page links every program's current round.
